paraphrase: Knowledge alone is one, eternal, without beginning or end; nothing else is real. The differences seen in the world are due to the limiting adjuncts of the senses; knowledge itself does not appear otherwise.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: Others hold that there are many eternal all-pervading selves; others that only what is perceived exists and there is no heaven; others that there is a stream of knowledge, or the void; others that reality is twofold, prakṛti and puruṣa; some say the world is without a Lord, others with a Lord — these contentious views cannot all be stated; those who wander among them are shut out of the path of liberation.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage. A doxography: the views correspond to Nyāya/Sāṃkhya selves, the Cārvāka, Buddhist views, Sāṃkhya dualism, atheist and theist schools (identifications are U28's reading, not stated by names in the text).
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: Having examined all the śāstras and reflected again and again, this one system of yoga is established as supreme; when it is known all is known; this secret yogaśāstra is to be given only to a true devotee.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: Some praise truth, others austerity, purity, forbearance or straightforwardness; some gifts, ancestral rites, action or dispassion; some the duties of the householder, the Agnihotra, mantrayoga or pilgrimage — people settled in such views are deluded and wander helplessly through the round of birth and death.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: Knowing by scripture and reasoning that the world is the play of māyā, yogins bring it to dissolution by superimposition and its withdrawal (adhyāropa-apavāda).
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: Bindu is Śiva and rajas is Śakti; from the union of the two, by their own inert power, arise the elements as in a dream.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: In this body is Mount Meru with the seven continents, rivers, oceans, mountains, fields and their guardians, seers, sages, stars and planets, sacred fords, seats and their deities; the moon and sun, agents of creation and dissolution, move in it, and space, air, fire, water and earth; all beings in the three worlds are in the body, and all activity proceeds around Meru. He who knows this is a yogin.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: There are three hundred and fifty thousand channels in the human body, of which fourteen are principal; of the three chief ones suṣumnā alone is the foremost, dear to yogins; within it is the channel citrā, beloved of Śiva, and in it the subtle brahmarandhra.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: On the peak of Meru within the body is the moon with eight kalās, facing downward, raining nectar day and night; the nectar divides: one part goes through iḍā to nourish the body; at the base of Meru is the sun with twelve kalās, which moves upward by the right path and swallows the nectar and the bodily constituents.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: In the heart is a divine lotus adorned with a divine liṅga and the twelve letters from ka to ṭha; there dwells prāṇa, decked with latent impressions, bound by beginningless karma and joined to egoism. By its different functions the breath has ten principal names — prāṇa, apāna, samāna, udāna, vyāna, nāga, kūrma, kṛkara, devadatta, dhanañjaya — of which prāṇa and apāna are chief; prāṇa in the heart, apāna in the anus, samāna in the navel, udāna in the throat, vyāna pervading the body; nāga and the others cause belching, opening the eyes, hunger, yawning and hiccup.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: Knowledge that comes from the guru's mouth is potent; otherwise it is fruitless, impotent and very painful. Those who worship knowledge after carefully pleasing the guru obtain its fruit. The guru is father, mother and god; he is to be served in deed, thought and word; by the guru's grace every good is obtained.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: Success is certain for those with faith, not for others; not for those attached, the faithless, those who do not worship the guru or who keep much company. The first sign of success is the confidence that it will bear fruit; the second faith; the third worship of the guru; the fourth equanimity; the fifth restraint of the senses; the sixth moderate diet; there is no seventh.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: In a fine hut, seated on a seat in padmāsana, the yogin should practise the breath; with body straight and hands joined he bows to the gurus, to Gaṇeśa on the right and to Kṣetrapāla and Ambikā on the left; closing piṅgalā with the right thumb he fills through iḍā and holds as far as able, releases slowly through piṅgalā, then fills through piṅgalā, holds and releases slowly through iḍā; he does this at dawn, midday, sunset and midnight (with a stated number of retentions, not reproduced), free of sloth, for three months; then the channels are surely purified.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: In the stage of beginning (ārambha) the yogin's body becomes harmonious, fragrant and lustrous, his voice perfected. The four stages in all yogas are ārambha, ghaṭa, paricaya and niṣpatti. (In the beginning stage) the yogin gains strong digestion, good enjoyment, happiness, beauty of all limbs, fullness of heart, enthusiasm and strength.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.

paraphrase: The yogin should give up theft, harming, hatred of people, egoism, crookedness, fasting, falsehood, (the thought of) liberation, cruelty to creatures, the company of women, tending fire, much talk, likes and dislikes, and overeating.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage. paraphrase: Aids to quick success: constant listening to doctrine, dwelling in a house of dispassion, chanting the name of Viṣṇu, listening to sweet sound, fortitude, forbearance, austerity, purity, modesty, intelligence and service of the guru — these observances the yogin should always follow.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.

paraphrase: The wise do not practise immediately after eating nor when hungry; in the first period of practice one should take milk and ghee; when the practice is firm such restriction is not needed; the practitioner should eat a little at a time, several times.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: At the first effort sweat appears and should be rubbed into the body; in the second stage trembling; in the middle stage hopping like a frog; with further practice the practitioner moves in the sky — even seated in padmāsana he leaves the ground: this is mastery of the breath. Then sleep, faeces and urine become scant; the yogin is free of disease and dejection; sweat, saliva and worms do not arise; he may eat little or much without harm.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.

paraphrase: There are many terrible obstacles, hard to avert; still the yogin should persevere even with his life in his throat. Then, seated in solitude with senses restrained, he should repeat the long praṇava to destroy the obstacles.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)
alt_notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: When the ghaṭa stage arises in the practice of the breath, there is nothing in the wheel of saṃsāra he cannot achieve. Because prāṇa and apāna, nāda and bindu, the jīvātman and the paramātman meet (ghaṭate) together, it is called ghaṭa. When he is able to hold the breath for a long time (the text states a period, not reproduced), then there is pratyāhāra: whatever the yogin knows he should regard as the self; with whatever senses and in whatever way, he conquers those senses.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Then by practice the stage of familiarity (paricaya) arises: the breath leaves the moon and sun and stays motionless in the space of suṣumnā; taking hold of the power of action (kriyāśakti) it pierces the centres, and the yogin sees the three peaks of his karma.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)
alt_notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: At this time the great yogin should practise the fivefold concentration (dhāraṇā), by which mastery over earth and the other elements comes and fear of the elements is removed: (holding the breath) at the base, at the place of the liṅga, above that, at the navel-heart region, and above the brows (for periods the text states); the wise one who practises the concentration of all the elements has no death even after a hundred deaths of Brahmā.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Then by the progression of practice consummation (niṣpatti) comes to the yogin; by it he crosses the seeds of beginningless karma and drinks the nectar; for the calm, steadfast yogin liberated while living, samādhi arises at will; the breath, taking consciousness and the power of action, conquers all the centres and dissolves in the power of knowledge.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)
alt_notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Practices of 'drinking the breath' for removing afflictions: placing the tongue at the root of the palate and drinking the breath; drinking cool air through the crow's-beak mouth (with knowledge of prāṇa and apāna); pressing the cavity at the root of the front teeth; drinking with the teeth pressed together and the tongue upward. The text claims these destroy fatigue, burning, old age and disease, that with the tongue upward drinking the moon's water one conquers death in a month, and that after long practice one becomes like Bhairava, gains the powers such as aṇimā and is not stained by merit or sin.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: There are eighty-four postures of many kinds; from them four have been taken and are taught: siddhāsana, then padmāsana, the fierce posture (ugra) and svastika.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Siddhāsana: pressing the perineum carefully with the heel and placing the other heel above the penis, gazing upward between the brows, motionless, senses restrained; by practising it one quickly reaches completion in yoga; the breath-practitioner should always use it; there is no posture more secret on earth, and by merely contemplating it the yogin is freed from sin.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Padmāsana: the feet placed soles-up on the thighs, the hands palms-up between the thighs, the gaze on the nose-tip, the tongue at the root of the teeth, the chin raised (or set) on the chest, drawing in the breath slowly; it destroys all diseases and is obtained only by the wise; when it is done the breath at once moves evenly; the yogin in padmāsana who fills (with breath) by the method of prāṇa and apāna is liberated.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: The fierce posture (ugrāsana): stretching both legs apart without touching, holding them firmly with the hands and placing the head on the knees — this kindles the breath, removes bodily decline and is called paścimottāna; for one who practises it daily the breath moves by the back path; all success comes to its practitioners; it is to be kept secret.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Svastika: holding both soles properly between the knees and thighs, the body straight, sitting comfortably; by it the wise yogin masters the breath and no disease enters the body; it is called the comfortable posture (sukhāsana), removing all pain; svastika, the best of auspicious things, is to be kept secret by yogins.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Yoni mudrā: first by inhalation one fills the base (ādhāra) with the mind and contracts the yoni between the anus and the genitals; one meditates on Kāma in the brahma-yoni, like a ball, bright as millions of suns and cool as millions of moons, above it a subtle flame of consciousness, which goes by the path of Brahman through the three liṅgas to the nectar in heaven and returns to the kula by the measured yoga. By this binding there is nothing that cannot be accomplished: even mantras that are 'cut', 'nailed', 'paralysed', 'burnt' or otherwise defective become effective; one bound by yoni mudrā is not stained by the killing of a thousand brahmins, of the guru, drinking liquor, theft or the violation of the guru's bed. It is to be practised daily by those seeking liberation and not given to anyone even at the cost of life.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text. The praise of its sin-removing power is an arthavāda in the text's own manner.

paraphrase: Therefore, to awaken the goddess (īśvarī) sleeping at the mouth of the brahmarandhra, one should practise the mudrās with every effort.
notes: Ref checked against the local e-text (Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Mallinson 2007) number differently); paraphrase by U28-hatha-texts from the passage. Parallel to HYP 3.5.
speaker: Īśvara (Śiva)

paraphrase: Mahāmudrā, mahābandha, mahāvedha, khecarī, jālandhara, mūlabandha, viparītakaraṇī, uḍḍāna, vajrolī and, tenth, śakticālana — these are the ten mudrās.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text. The Muktabodha e-text names 'vajroṇī' in the list but has no vajrolī section; other editions include one.

paraphrase: Mahāmudrā, by which Kapila and the siddhas of old attained success: pressing the perineum with the left heel as the guru teaches, holding the stretched right leg with both hands, restraining the nine doors and placing the chin on the chest, setting the mind on the path of mind — this secret mahāmudrā is done on the left then the right side; by it even the unfortunate yogin succeeds; it moves all the channels, 'kills' bindu, revives the impure and destroys sins; it is to be kept secret, a wish-fulfilling cow for practitioners.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Mahābandha: placing the stretched leg on the thigh, contracting the anus and yoni, making apāna go upward and joining it with samāna, turning prāṇa downward, one binds (them) for the upward movement; by practice the breath goes into the middle of the suṣumnā, the body is nourished, the skeleton firmly bound and the heart full; it is to be done with both legs.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Mahāvedha: having united apāna and prāṇa and filled the belly with breath, one seated in mahāvedha gently strikes the buttocks; by this piercing, with the breath, the yogin pierces the brahma-knot through the path of the suṣumnā; the gods in the centres tremble at the striking of the breath and kuṇḍalinī, the great māyā, dissolves in Kailāsa. Mahāmudrā and mahābandha are fruitless without mahāvedha, so the yogin performs all three in order; the siddha alone knows their greatness; they are to be kept secret, for otherwise there is no success in the mudrās.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: RESTRICTED — summary only: khecarī is described as sitting in vajrāsana with the gaze firmly between the brows and joining the tongue, turned back, to the cavity above the uvula, the 'well of nectar'; the text says it is the mother of powers, that by it one drinks nectar daily and gains bodily perfection, that the one whose khecarī is pure is pure whatever his state, and that it is to be given to no one. The preparatory procedure is not reproduced.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Jālandhara: binding the network of channels at the throat, placing the chin on the chest — hard even for the gods. The fire at the navel of creatures drinks the nectar falling from the thousand-petalled lotus; to prevent this one binds this lock, and by it the wise one drinks the nectar himself and, gaining immortality, rejoices in the three worlds.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Mūlabandha: pressing the anal passage well with the heel and forcibly drawing up apāna, moving it gradually upward — this destroys old age and death; it unites apāna and prāṇa, and by it yoni mudrā succeeds; by its grace the yogin, seated in padmāsana, leaves the ground; it is to be practised in a well-hidden, solitary place by one who would cross the ocean of saṃsāra.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Viparītakaraṇī: placing the head on the ground and raising the two feet into the air — secret in all the tantras; one who practises it daily for a watch conquers death, does not perish even at the dissolution, drinks the nectar and becomes equal to the siddhas.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: Uḍḍiyāna: drawing the belly back above and below the navel — this lock removes all sorrow, the lion to the elephant of death; practised daily (at stated times) the navel is purified, the breath is mastered, the fire in the belly blazes and the vital fluid increases; in six months one conquers death; the body is perfected and diseases destroyed; it is to be learned from the guru and practised in a solitary place.
notes: Ref per Śivasaṃhitā, Muktabodha e-text M00082 (Varanasi 1928 printing); numbering of that e-text — other editions (e.g. Vasu; Mallinson 2007) number differently and include a vajrolī section absent from this e-text.

paraphrase: RESTRICTED — summary only: śakticālana is described as moving the kuṇḍalī asleep in the base lotus by forcibly drawing up apāna; the text says that by daily practice life is lengthened and diseases destroyed, the serpent leaves sleep and rises of herself, and success comes to one who practises it by the guru's instruction; the duration and procedure are not reproduced.

paraphrase: Aspirants are of four kinds: mild (mṛdu), middling (madhya), strong (adhimātra) and strongest (adhimātratama), the last able to cross the ocean of existence. The mild — fickle, timid, sick, dependent, harsh, of slack conduct and little vigour — is fit for mantrayoga and succeeds in twelve years; the middling — even-minded, forbearing, seeking merit, kind in speech, moderate in all things — is given layayoga; the strong — brave, youthful, faithful, worshipping the guru's feet, devoted to practice — is given haṭhayoga with its limbs and succeeds in six years; the strongest — detached from company, free of great disease, of strong vows — is fit for all the yogas and succeeds in three years.

paraphrase: Worship of one's reflection (pratīkopāsana) gives seen and unseen fruits: in bright sunshine, gazing with wide eyes at the Lord reflected as one's own shadow and then at the sky, one sees one's own image in the sky; seeing it daily lengthens life and removes death; seeing it whole brings victory. One should do it at the time of journeys, marriage, auspicious acts, danger, and for the destruction of sin and increase of merit.

paraphrase: Rājayoga: above is the divine thousand-petalled lotus, outside the body called brahmāṇḍa, bestowing liberation; it is called Kailāsa, where the great Lord (Maheśa) dwells, imperishable, free of waxing and waning. The yogin whose mind rests there, in the abode of the haṃsa, lives long, free of disease and death. He should constantly drink the nectar that flows from there; kuṇḍalinī, called Kulā, dissolves there, and then the fourfold creation is dissolved in the supreme self.

paraphrase: Without haṭha there is no rājayoga, and without rājayoga no haṭha; therefore the yogin should proceed in haṭha by the path of a true guru.

paraphrase: Company must be abandoned entirely, otherwise there is no liberation; the practice is done in secret, inwardly renouncing company while outwardly acting for the sake of worldly dealings. Resolving thus, even a householder who practises attains success; freed of sin and merit, abiding at home, the householder joined in yoga is not stained by sin or merit even when acting for his own ends and the welfare of the world.

paraphrase: Now the excellent mantra-practice that gives happiness in this world and the next: in the four-petalled lotus of the root-support shines the seed of speech (vāgbhava), brilliant as lightning (seed-syllables printed in the e-text at the head of the passage: aiṃ, klīṃ, strīṃ).

paraphrase: Obstacles to liberation are of three kinds. Those in the form of enjoyment (bhoga) — learning, the Vedas and śāstras, dance, song, ornaments, instruments, elephants and horses, wife, children and sense-objects; those in the form of dharma — the object of meditation, meditation, mantra, gifts, fame, wells and tanks, temples and gardens, sacrifices, the Cāndrāyaṇa and Kṛcchra vows and pilgrimages; and those in the form of knowledge — (mistaken) practices and notions (listed in 5.5–8).

paraphrase: Therefore the best of yogins should act by the prescribed method, content with what comes unsought; even a householder, unattached, is liberated by the practice of yoga. Householders gain success by the repetition of the Lord's names joined to yogic practice; living at home, full of wife and children, abandoning attachment inwardly on the path of yoga, the householder, having seen the signs of success, may enjoy himself, having accomplished my teaching.

paraphrase: Closing both ears with the thumbs, the eyes with the index fingers, the nostrils with the middle fingers and the mouth firmly with the ring fingers, restraining the breath, the yogin sees the self as light; whoever sees that light even for a moment is freed of all sins and reaches the supreme goal; by constant practice he forgets the body and becomes one with it; practised secretly it merges one in Brahman; this yoga, dear to Śiva, gives immediate conviction; then the nāda arises gradually.

paraphrase: The first sound is like that of intoxicated bees, flute and vīṇā; then, by practice, a sound like a bell and then like the rumble of clouds, which destroys the darkness of saṃsāra; when one sets the mind on that sound and stays fearless, laya arises; the mind delighting in nāda forgets everything outward and becomes still with the nāda; by this practice, having overcome the many qualities, abandoning all undertakings, one dissolves in the space of consciousness.

paraphrase: There is no posture like siddha, no power like retention, no mudrā like khecarī and no dissolution like nāda.

paraphrase: Seated in padmāsana, recollecting the pit of the throat and placing the tongue at the root of the palate, the yogin's hunger and thirst cease; below the pit of the throat is the lovely kūrma-channel; fixing the mind there he gains great steadiness of mind.

paraphrase: Yoga is of four kinds: mantrayoga, haṭha, layayoga as the third, and the fourth, rājayoga, which is free of duality.
